clue.text: Retired in the main

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and water that has retired there is tide that has drawn back from the shore

explanation.surface: Someone has gone into retirement in the main part of their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work, and 'the main' sounds like 'mainly'; read as the sea, retiring water is a falling tide.
explanation.definitionFit: When a tide flows back out to sea it goes down the shore, which is exactly what the sea retiring means.

clue.text: Makes hostile sergeants change

indicators.note: change means the letters of sergeants are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Sergeants who alter their ways turn people against them.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to turn them from friend to unfriendly.

clue.text: Do vote against!

definitions.meaning: a do is a party or celebration
split up, the letters suggest '...', the instruction to vote against

explanation.definitionFit: A beano is a lively party or knees-up, and taken in pieces it urges one to cast a negative ballot.

clue.text: 22 ac, is really boring

definitions.meaning: the answer to 22 across is physical training, as soldiers do on the parade ground
boring means making holes with a tool

explanation.definitionFit: Military drill is a form of training, and a drill bores holes in wood or rock.

clue.text: Note submission when times are hard

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cession is a yielding or surrender of rights, a submission

explanation.surface: A memo about handing something over arrives during bad times.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic downturn is the period of hard times when trade shrinks.

clue.text: Rugby union not out for defeat

parts.note: a batsman not out in cricket is still in

explanation.surface: Rugby players who are still batting suffer a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is 'not out' is still IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Downfall or destruction, the complete overthrow of someone.

clue.text: A businessman's swindle over agricultural machinery

indicators.note: over means placed above, the swindle written first in this down answer

parts.note: a con is a swindle or confidence trick
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A trader cheats someone over the sale of farm equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder or tradesperson who takes on work under agreed terms runs a business.

clue.text: Boxes with a key are scarce

parts.note: to box is to spar, practise fighting
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Locked boxes are hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' reads as containers; here it is the verb, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly spread and few in number, hard to find.

clue.text: Inadequate, so' tense

definitions.meaning: in grammar a verb tense describing continuing past action

explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed falls short of perfection, and the grammatical name for continuous past action is a tense.

clue.text: Relative egghead in congenial situation

indicators.note: in means the egghead letter is placed inside the word for congenial

parts.note: nice means pleasant or congenial
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A family member who is a clever intellectual feels at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' means an intellectual; read as 'egg head' it is E. 'situation' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: The usual procedure is to drain it off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters of to drain it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Draining the vessel is just what is customarily done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' sits at the end looking like part of 'drain it off', but it signals the anagram of TO DRAIN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom handed down is the way things are customarily done.

clue.text: Politician framed by porter being generous

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the politician sits inside the beer

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP is surrounded by a doorman who is being kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' reads as a doorman or carrier; here it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plentiful and more than enough is lavish, like a generous serving.

clue.text: Greek god's head set in a ring

indicators.note: set in means the head is placed inside the a-and-ring pair

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax

explanation.surface: A deity's head is mounted in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun god of music and prophecy in the Olympian pantheon.

clue.text: Retain petty cash book

parts.note: small change is pennies, and P is the abbreviation for a penny
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Keep hold of the ledger for small office expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'petty cash book' looks like one office ledger; split it into P for a penny and 'book' for RESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something safe and unchanged is to hold on to it.

clue.text: Keeps old husband totally idle

parts.note: a shop that stocks goods keeps them
to husband land in the old sense is to cultivate it, to till it

explanation.surface: An elderly spouse holds on and does nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' looks like a spouse; it is the old verb meaning to farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely motionless, not moving a muscle.

clue.text: Sort of break for environmentalists — a very short time

parts.note: Greens are environmentalist campaigners or party members
a tick is a moment, as in 'back in a tick'

explanation.surface: Green campaigners take only a moment to break something.
explanation.walkthrough: A greenstick fracture is a partial bone break common in children.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for an incomplete fracture, where a young bone bends and cracks on one side.

clue.text: A ballet performance of "The Trance" perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the quoted title could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dance show could be titled after a hypnotic state.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'The Trance' look like a ballet's title; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap in ballet in which the dancer beats the calves together in the air.

clue.text: An enchanting creature responsible for endless insecurity

indicators.note: endless means the word for insecurity loses its final letter

parts.note: peril is danger, a state of insecurity

explanation.surface: A charming being is blamed for never-ending anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a beautiful fairy or sprite.

clue.text: Spreads out in folds

parts.note: creases are folds or lines in fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric unfolds from its pleats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreads out' must be read as 'grows', not 'unfolds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grows larger, expanding in size or number.

clue.text: New variety of corn — said to be bitter

indicators.note: a new variety reshapes something, so the letters of corn and said are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly bred cereal is reported to taste sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a link to 'be bitter'; it is part of the fodder with CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and cynical, scornful in a biting way.

clue.text: Situation calling for sound vision

indicators.note: sound means the word for vision is heard, giving a word that is spelt differently

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A location needs good eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy vision; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or position where something is placed.

clue.text: Such achievements may well be recognised by degrees

definitions.text: Such achievements may well be recognised by degrees

parts.words: Such achievements may well be recognised by degrees
parts.note: 'by degrees' seems to mean gradually, but here it means university degrees awarded for academic success

explanation.surface: Some accomplishments only gain recognition slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic accomplishments are rewarded with university qualifications.

clue.text: Fabulous birds turned up without concerning the successful batsman

indicators.note: turned up means read upwards in a down answer, here turning both the birds and the word for concerning that stands without (beside) them

parts.note: rocs are giant birds of legend in the Arabian Nights
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Legendary birds appeared, but nothing to do with the batsman who made runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived'; with 'without' it turns ROCS to SCOR and RE to ER, each in place.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the batsman who makes runs adds to the tally, putting points on the board.

clue.text: Work out tax without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the tax wraps the hesitation

parts.note: excise is a duty levied on goods
er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Calculate the duty owed without stalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean 'lacking'; here it means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to train the body, to do a workout at the gym.

clue.text: Uniform in fine quality material

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the words fine quality

explanation.surface: Clothing uniform is made from good cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' and 'material' paint a clothing picture; 'Uniform' means even, the same throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and the same everywhere, alike in every respect.

clue.text: Much like military personnel succeeding amid chaos

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the soldiers follow
chaos means the letters of amid are thrown into disorder

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Something resembles soldiers coming through in the middle of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: To like something much is to think highly of it, to hold it in esteem.

clue.text: A woman showing indignation over nurse being heartless

indicators.note: over places the anger above the nurse letters in this down answer

parts.note: ire is anger or indignation

indicators.note: heartless means the inside of the word nurse is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An angry woman shouts at an uncaring nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, here standing for any woman.

clue.text: Writer's work for which the fee is about a pound

indicators.note: is about means the fee goes around the pound

parts.note: pay is payment, a fee
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An author is paid about a pound for a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes stage drama for performance.

clue.text: American woman pilot

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A female American flier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' suggests flying; here it is a verb, to guide someone to their seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot someone is to guide or escort them, as an attendant leads people to seats.

clue.text: When one expresses disparagement they're quite detached

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to slander is to speak ill of someone

explanation.surface: When somebody runs others down, people keep their distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: island dwellers live on land quite detached from the mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: People who live on islands are separated by water from everyone else.

clue.text: Last-minute improvement, in an oblique way

parts.note: late describes something done at the last minute
a rally is a recovery or improvement, as in share prices

explanation.surface: A late recovery comes about by indirect means.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways rather than straight on is going at a slant.

clue.text: Child getting a letter and a game

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A youngster receives some post and something to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a letter' suggests post arriving; here it is the name of the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game of strategy played with kings, queens and pawns.
